cards.back: Causing another to apprehend immediate unlawful force (words/silence can suffice – Ireland)
Intentional or reckless application of unlawful force; can be indirect (Haystead)
s. 39 CJA 1988 – summary only
Only that of the assault/battery; no foresight of harm needed (Savage; Roberts)
Hurt/injury interfering with health or comfort, more than transient (Miller); psychiatric injury; cutting hair (DPP v Smith 2006)
Break in both layers of the skin (JCC v Eisenhower); inner skin of mouth counts
Really serious harm (DPP v Smith 1961); look at whole injuries and victim (Bollom)
Intention or recklessness as to SOME harm (Cunningham; Savage/Parmenter)
Intent to do GBH OR to resist/prevent lawful apprehension – specific intent, life max
No consent to ABH or worse, except recognised exceptions
Sport, surgery, tattooing/piercing, rough horseplay (Jones), informed risk of infection
Consent to serious harm for sexual gratification is no defence (ABH+)
England: only for common assault/battery – not ABH+. Abolished in Wales (2022)
Reasonable force in circumstances as D believed them; householder: grossly disproportionate never reasonable
Threat without lawful excuse, intending the person to fear it would be carried out
SCA 2015 s. 75A – no injury needed
heroin, cocaine/crack, MDMA, LSD, methadone, methamphetamine, magic mushrooms
cannabis, amphetamine, ketamine, codeine, mephedrone, synthetic cannabinoids
benzodiazepines, GHB/GBL, anabolic steroids, khat
Must know you have the thing (package); s. 28 deals with knowledge of the drug
Quantity must be visible, tangible, measurable
Supply/offer; being concerned in supply by another; being concerned in making an offer
Complete when made – even without drugs or with fake drugs
Possession with intent to supply
Cultivation of cannabis
Occupier/manager knowingly permits: produce, supply, prepare opium, SMOKE cannabis/opium
Took possession to prevent offence → destroy/deliver ASAP; or to deliver to lawful custody
Didn't know/suspect/have reason to suspect it was a controlled drug; mistaken drug type is no defence
Reasonable grounds to suspect possession → search/detain person, search vehicle, seize
Both 16+, personally connected, abusive behaviour (physical/sexual, violent/threatening, controlling/coercive, economic, psychological/emotional)
Married/civil partners, engaged, intimate relationship, parental relationship to same child, relatives
See, hear or experience effects → victims
Repeated/continuous controlling or coercive behaviour; serious effect; knows or ought to know
Fear of violence on ≥2 occasions OR serious alarm/distress with substantial adverse effect on day-to-day
Best interests + reasonable – not if fear of violence
Superintendent; magistrates within 48 h; DVPO 14–28 days
DAA 2021 replacements (roll-out ⚠)
Right to ask / right to know
Risk assessment → multi-agency meeting for high risk
